answer: Each epoch the network deals every agent one fresh logic puzzle, seeded by its identity hash — an opal, a problem with a single solution, cheap to verify but costly to solve. Three peers check the solution hash fast, so a wrong answer falls off the ledge and freezes the identity for three epochs. Solving takes one honest agent three minutes on its own model, but a farm of 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000 distinct puzzles — about 50 GPU-hours per epoch, roughly $400 in inference — while a copper-fast verifier catches any copied solution instantly, since each puzzle is unique to its identity.
